newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF REAL MADRID PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF REAL MADRID PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the Real Madrid players most likely to play against Atletico Madrid in Saturday's Spanish league match:

Bodo Illgner, goalkeeper, 29. A surprise signing at the beginning of the season after Capello demanded a taller keeper, the former German international has become one of the mainstays of the Real side since ousting Canizares and veteran Paco Buyo.

Santiago Canizares, goalkeeper, 28. Kept Spain's World Cup qualification hopes alive against Denmark in 1993, but is now thought to be anxious to move on since playing second fiddle to Buyo and then to Illgner since joining Real from Celta Vigo.
Carlos Secretario, defender, 27. Portuguese international who was replaced by Panucci earlier in the season. The absence of left-back Roberto Carlos may give Secretario his chance.

Rafael Alkorta, defender, 28. A regular in the national side and ever-present at the heart of the Real defence this season, Alkorta is one of the toughest markers in Spain. Set to move to Athletic Bilbao next season.

Fernando Hierro, defender, 29. The tower on which the Real defence is built, Hierro comes forward well and is strong in the air at set-pieces and can be lethal at free kicks. Under his new contract, Hierro's salary is thought to be 300 million pesetas.
Chendo Porlan, defender 35. Veteran defender who has been playing for Real since 1983. Chendo is an unlikely starter, but always a reliable substitute.

Christian Panucci, defender, 24. Has slotted straight into the Real line-up since making his debut on the right of defence after signing from AC Milan for around 700 million pesetas ($5.34 million) in December. Dangerous in the air at corners.
Fernando Sanz, defender, 23. Substitute defender who is still trying to escape the shadow of being the son of Real president Lorenzo Sanz.
Luis Milla, midfielder, 31. Milla's signing from Barcelona sent shock-waves through the Spanish game back in 1990, but he has since fallen from favour, and is an unlikely starter.
Manuel Sanchis, midfielder, 32. Son of a 1960s Real star, Sanchis had been a regular first team choice in both defence and midfield since 1983, but has struggled to impress Capello.

Fernando Redondo, midfielder, 27. Argentine international with a delicate touch, the injury-prone Redondo is yet to find his form this season after missing seven months league action. Thought likely to follow coach Capello to AC Milan.

Clarence Seedorf, midfielder, 21. Surinam-born Dutch international whose busy support work behind the front men has made him an unsung hero since signing from Sampdoria in the close season. Has found his goal touch in recent games.

Victor Sanchez, midfielder, 21. Quietly efficient midfielder whose work down the right and powerful shot has earnt him occasional promotion from Real's B team. Scored a superb goal earlier this season against Atletico, but is likely to be kept on the bench in favour of Amavisca.

Emilio Amavisca, midfielder/striker, 25. A skilful support player rather than goalscorer who has recently returned after missing several months through injury. Amavisca failed disastrously as an improvised left-back in Spain's World Cup qualifier against the Czech Republic last weekend.

Raul Gonzalez, midfielder/striker, 19. Extraordinarily mature 19-year-old who continues to improve despite playing out of position in the left side of midfield since the arrival of Suker and Mijatovic. A true match-winner, Raul carried his side in the memorable 4-1 over Atletico in January.

Davor Suker, striker, 29. The Croatian Euro 96 star has shone since signing from Sevilla. Heavily left-sided, Suker can take on men and beat them before unleashing a powerful shot. Strong at set-pieces. Suker has recently bet a million pesetas (nearly $7,000) that he will stay at Real next season.

Predrag Mijatovic, striker, 28. The Montenegrino's lethal right foot made him Spain's second-highest goalscorer at Valencia last season. Has moved into attack after starting in midfield. Often accused of diving in the penalty area, he was sent off for insulting the referee in the last derby game.
